grind_in_grass.description: Generates a list of overworld movement buttons to walk back and forth along a specified horizontal coordinate range to trigger wild encounters.

left_x.description: The left boundary of the horizontal grinding path.

right_x.description: The right boundary of the horizontal grinding path.

y_row.description: The Y-coordinate/row where the grinding path lies.

num_passes.description: The number of one-way sweeps (left-to-right or right-to-left) to perform.

grind_in_grass.python_script:
import json

# Retrieve input arguments
curr_x = int(input_data['curr_x'])
curr_y = int(input_data['curr_y'])
left_x = int(input_data['left_x'])
right_x = int(input_data['right_x'])
y_row = int(input_data['y_row'])
num_passes = int(input_data['num_passes'])

buttons = []

# Verify we are on the correct row. If not, don't generate overworld buttons to prevent wrong movements.
if curr_y != y_row:
    # Print empty list and message in output
    print(json.dumps([]))
else:
    # Start pacing
    current_pos = curr_x
    direction = "Left" if current_pos > left_x else "Right"
    
    for _ in range(num_passes):
        if direction == "Left":
            steps = current_pos - left_x
            buttons.extend(["Left"] * steps)
            current_pos = left_x
            direction = "Right"
        else:
            steps = right_x - current_pos
            buttons.extend(["Right"] * steps)
            current_pos = right_x
            direction = "Left"
            
    # Max button presses constraint (100)
    buttons = buttons[:100]
    print(json.dumps(buttons))

history.commit_message: Initial definition of grind_in_grass tool to automate overworld wild encounter searching by pacing back and forth in a designated horizontal line of grass.

safari_pathfinder.description: Calculates the shortest valid overworld path (sequence of buttons) between two coordinates in any Safari Zone map, taking into account verified obstacles, plateaus, and lake boundaries.

map_id.description: The current map ID (e.g. '0_220' for Center, '0_217' for East, '0_218' for North, '0_219' for West).

safari_pathfinder.python_script:
import json
import collections

# Extract input parameters safely
map_id = input_data['map_id']
start_x = int(input_data['start_x'])
start_y = int(input_data['start_y'])
target_x = int(input_data['target_x'])
target_y = int(input_data['target_y'])

def find_path():
    width = 30
    height = 30
    impassable = set()

    if map_id == "0_220":  # Safari Zone Center
        # Gatehouse fence
        for x in range(0, 30):
            if x != 14:
                impassable.add((x, 25))
        for x in [13, 15, 16]:
            impassable.add((x, 24))

        # Rest House 1
        for x in range(16, 20):
            for y in range(18, 21):
                impassable.add((x, y))
        impassable.add((18, 20))

        # Row 15/16 tree/fence wall (from Col 2 to Col 17)
        for y in [15, 16]:
            for x in range(2, 18):
                impassable.add((x, y))

        # Western border trees on Rows 16-17
        for x in [0, 1]:
            for y in [16, 17]:
                impassable.add((x, y))
        for x in range(2, 6):
            impassable.add((x, 16))

        # Row 9 fence (Columns 22 to 27) and trees (28-29)
        for x in range(22, 30):
            impassable.add((x, 9))
        for x in [28, 29]:
            impassable.add((x, 8))

        # Central Lake (Rows 8 to 13, Columns 8 to 21)
        # Note: on screen we also saw Row 10 water on 18-21
        for y in range(8, 14):
            for x in range(8, 22):
                impassable.add((x, y))

        # Additional fence posts on Row 14
        impassable.add((19, 14))
        impassable.add((13, 14))
        impassable.add((10, 14))

    elif map_id == "0_217":  # Safari Zone East
        # Southern boundary
        for x in range(0, 30):
            impassable.add((x, 25))

        # Northern tree canopy (Rows 18-20)
        for y in [18, 19, 20]:
            for x in range(1, 7):
                impassable.add((x, y))

        # Rest House 2 (Columns 5-8, Row 23) and surrounding posts
        for x in range(5, 9):
            impassable.add((x, 23))
        impassable.add((6, 22))
        impassable.add((6, 21))
        impassable.add((10, 21)) # Tree/post on Row 21 Col 10

        # Plateau Cliff constraints:
        # Plateau is Columns 11-22, Rows 18-20.
        # Cliff edges are Row 21 (Col 11-19, 21-22).
        # We can walk horizontally only on Row 20 (or Row 18/19), not Row 21.
        for x in range(11, 23):
            if x != 20: # 20 is the stairs up
                impassable.add((x, 21))

    elif map_id == "0_218":  # Safari Zone North
        # Row 34 fence/building
        for x in range(10, 20):
            impassable.add((x, 34))

    elif map_id == "0_219":  # Safari Zone West
        # Column 1 blockages
        impassable.add((1, 15))
        impassable.add((1, 14))
        impassable.add((0, 16))
        
        # Lake water blockages
        impassable.add((2, 13))
        impassable.add((3, 13))
        for x in range(4, 9):
            impassable.add((x, 13))

        # Column 24 tree wall blockage
        for y in range(1, 13):
            impassable.add((24, y))

    # Standard BFS
    queue = collections.deque([(start_x, start_y, [])])
    visited = set([(start_x, start_y)])

    while queue:
        cx, cy, path = queue.popleft()
        if (cx, cy) == (target_x, target_y):
            return path
        for dx, dy, move in [(0, -1, "Up"), (0, 1, "Down"), (-1, 0, "Left"), (1, 0, "Right")]:
            nx, ny = cx + dx, cy + dy
            if 0 <= nx < width and 0 <= ny < height and (nx, ny) not in impassable and (nx, ny) not in visited:
                visited.add((nx, ny))
                queue.append((nx, ny, path + [move]))
    return None

path = find_path()
if path is not None:
    print(json.dumps(path))
else:
    print(json.dumps([]))

history.commit_message: Create a robust Safari Zone pathfinder tool that calculates optimal movement paths bypassing all verified static obstacles.
